title: seri.ai 24-Dimension Quality Scorecard
rule: A score reaches 10 only when current evidence shows no material gap against the intended world-class technical publication and professional representation bar.

dimensions.name: Professional Representation
dimensions.evidence: Home, Start Here, Work, Background, Resume, GitHub, LinkedIn, contact paths, the First-Time Visitor Review Kit, Practitioner Review Packet, portrait intake contract, durable first-viewport screenshots, and a durable non-photographic public identity mark make Ravikanth Seri visible as the author and engineer behind the work.
dimensions.gap: An approved portrait photo and completed external first-impression review are still missing, so the person-work-evidence path is not yet independently validated.
dimensions.nextProof: Add the approved portrait photo through /identity/portrait-intake.md when available, then run the Practitioner Review Packet with external reviewers at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.

dimensions.name: Career Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The professional graph, Background route, Start Here path, First-Time Visitor Review Kit, and Practitioner Review Packet show the arc from enterprise integration through cloud, observability, production AI systems, and Operational Intelligence.
dimensions.gap: The career story is strong in structured content but still needs completed reviewer feedback from people who know nothing about Ravikanth.
dimensions.nextProof: Run the Practitioner Review Packet with external reviewers and record where they become uncertain.

dimensions.name: Technical Authority
dimensions.evidence: Doctrine, Reference Architecture, Publication Pack, Evidence Pack, patterns, and Operations Room create a serious technical body of work.
dimensions.gap: Independent practitioner review and measured control-comparison results are still missing.
dimensions.nextProof: Collect practitioner reviews and publish dimension-level findings with limitations.

dimensions.name: Engineering Depth
dimensions.evidence: The site exposes layer contracts, state machines, evidence objects, hypothesis lifecycle, replay seeds, evaluation gates, and decision packets.
dimensions.gap: Most deep examples still orbit OI-ROOM-001; more distinct public-safe scenarios are needed.
dimensions.nextProof: Add only scenario fixtures that test new failure modes, not decorative examples.

dimensions.name: AI Systems Credibility
dimensions.evidence: Ask Ravikanth, deterministic trust fixtures, eval gates, local fallback behavior, AI-governance language, and a controlled Ask live review packet are present.
dimensions.gap: Live model synthesis quality, vector retrieval quality, and reviewer-labeled sessions are not yet proven.
dimensions.nextProof: Run the Ask live review packet to compare fallback, vector retrieval, and model synthesis on the same safe prompt set using reviewer labels and safe metadata only.

dimensions.name: Architecture Quality
dimensions.evidence: The Reference Architecture defines implementation-neutral contracts, state behavior, governance controls, and conformance profiles.
dimensions.gap: No independent team has implemented the doctrine from the specification yet.
dimensions.nextProof: Use a second public-safe implementation or external architecture review to test whether the contracts are precise.

dimensions.name: Publications
dimensions.evidence: The Library, wiki, articles, publication spine, RSS, changelog, and reference exports make the body of work navigable.
dimensions.gap: The platform needs more high-rigor field notes grounded in evidence, review, and counterexamples.
dimensions.nextProof: Strengthen existing canonical assets before adding new articles, and publish only when a note improves the doctrine.

dimensions.name: Originality
dimensions.evidence: Operational Intelligence is framed as original synthesis built on observability, SRE, incident response, knowledge graphs, and AI evaluation.
dimensions.gap: The distinction remains partly conceptual until practitioner review and control comparisons test it.
dimensions.nextProof: Use the Evidence Pack to show where the model adds value over adjacent modes and where it does not.

dimensions.name: Evidence Quality
dimensions.evidence: Resume provenance, public-code boundaries, doctrine citations, eval fixtures, proof backlog, First-Time Visitor Review Kit, Practitioner Review Packet, and evidence-led pages reduce unsupported claims.
dimensions.gap: The strongest remaining evidence is external: completed practitioner review, benchmark results, live telemetry, and visual QA artifacts.
dimensions.nextProof: Execute the proof backlog and review kit, then update claims only when new evidence supports them.

dimensions.name: Work / Project Proof
dimensions.evidence: Work, Projects, Artifacts, GitHub references, Sentinalai context, public-code review rubric, Operations Room, and the Public Project Proof Ledger now state what each project proves, what can be inspected, what it does not prove, and the next proof needed.
dimensions.gap: Project claims now have public-safe proof boundaries and public-code inspection rules, but public repositories still need deeper runnable examples, reviewer walkthroughs, or independent implementation feedback.
dimensions.nextProof: Improve the most representative public repository README and run the project proof review questions against external reviewers without inventing private metrics.

dimensions.name: Knowledge-Graph Health
dimensions.evidence: Content registry, professional graph, publishing index, related assets, search, and a repeatable knowledge-graph health validator now check 63 assets, 8038 relationships, 10 layers, 15 registry items, 10 patterns, and 10 principles.
dimensions.gap: The graph health gate now has automated orphan, relationship, duplicate-concept, and layer-coverage checks, but still needs periodic editorial review as the corpus grows and new external evidence arrives.
dimensions.nextProof: Run the knowledge-graph health validator after every publishing change and add reviewer-driven stale-fact or redundancy findings when real content growth exposes them.

dimensions.name: Ask Ravi
dimensions.evidence: Ask has public-safety refusal, citations, related routes, deterministic fallback, answer metadata, project-proof routing, public-code rubric routing, visitor-review routing, practitioner-review routing, visual-QA routing, credential-evidence routing, identity-asset and portrait-intake routing, mobile-touch evidence routing, keyboard-accessibility evidence routing, Ask live review packet routing, and 106 passing fixtures.
dimensions.gap: A controlled Ask live review packet exists, but no live reviewer-labeled answer quality baseline has been published across realistic professional, architecture, safety, and routing questions.
dimensions.nextProof: Run the Ask live review packet and publish qualitative labels without raw prompts or aggregate model-quality scores.

dimensions.name: Search / Discoverability
dimensions.evidence: Search covers registry, wiki, articles, patterns, projects, reference assets, resume credential evidence, public-code review rubric, project proof, proof backlog, visitor review, practitioner review, visual QA, identity asset, portrait intake, mobile touch walkthroughs, keyboard accessibility walkthroughs, Ask live review packet, and 66 canonical retrieval checks.
dimensions.gap: Live search-console evidence and real query behavior are not yet available.
dimensions.nextProof: After beta deployment, review crawler visibility and query impressions for doctrine, framework, and Operations Room pages.

dimensions.name: Visual Design
dimensions.evidence: The site has a restrained dark visual system, proof-led cards, diagram surfaces, performance-guarded rendered routes, 27 durable first-viewport screenshots, and source-validated mobile touch walkthrough notes for Ask, Operations Room, Doctrine, Radar, and Work.
dimensions.gap: The latest browser pass found no page-level horizontal overflow, and touch notes now exist, but dense technical surfaces still need external hierarchy and density review.
dimensions.nextProof: Run external visual review and physical-device checks, then fix any hierarchy, density, touch-comfort, or graph-framing issues found by reviewers.

dimensions.name: UX
dimensions.evidence: Start Here, primary CTAs, proof paths, Ask prompts, related reading, reference assets, the First-Time Visitor Review Kit, and the Practitioner Review Packet provide guided navigation.
dimensions.gap: The Operations Room and long reference pages still need more observed user-review evidence.
dimensions.nextProof: Run a 10-20 minute first-time visitor walkthrough and record where users hesitate.

dimensions.name: Mobile
dimensions.evidence: Viewport contracts, mobile quick prompts, responsive tables, mobile-friendly wiki contents, browser-controlled 390px/tablet checks, responsive section rhythm, responsive card density, contained Ask prompt grid, 390px screenshot artifacts for nine critical routes, and source-validated touch walkthrough notes for five dense routes are validated.
dimensions.gap: Physical-device touch comfort, scroll fatigue, and first-time reviewer hesitation points are still unproven.
dimensions.nextProof: Run real-device touch checks for Ask, Operations Room, Doctrine, Radar, and Work, then record hesitation points from external reviewers.

dimensions.name: Accessibility
dimensions.evidence: Automated accessibility validation covers semantic headings, labels, focus styling, reduced motion, navigation, graph fallbacks, and the Keyboard Accessibility Walkthrough Notes artifact for Ask and Operations Room. The evidence level is source-validated keyboard accessibility walkthrough notes, not a screen-reader lab run.
dimensions.gap: browser-recorded keyboard tab-order checks, screen-reader spot checks, and external assistive-technology review are still missing.
dimensions.nextProof: Run browser-recorded keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs for Ask and Operations Room, then encode any repeatable failures into validators.

dimensions.name: SEO
dimensions.evidence: Sitemap, robots, RSS, llms.txt, Open Graph images, canonical metadata, JSON-LD, and rendered metadata checks are present.
dimensions.gap: There is no live indexing, social-preview, search-console, or crawler feedback proving that external discovery works after deployment.
dimensions.nextProof: Inspect public deployment indexing and social previews after beta traffic begins.

dimensions.name: Performance
dimensions.evidence: Production build, static generation, rendered-route validation, and performance budgets pass.
dimensions.gap: Operations Room remains the heaviest route and needs measured interaction latency on real devices.
dimensions.nextProof: Measure route and interaction latency on preview or production devices after beta deployment.

dimensions.name: Reliability
dimensions.evidence: API timeouts, rate limiting, fallbacks, local build gates, route validation, and runbook guidance exist.
dimensions.gap: Live uptime, Ask latency, fallback rate, and contact persistence evidence are not yet available.
dimensions.nextProof: Review Vercel logs and privacy-safe analytics after real beta traffic, then publish latency, fallback, and error limitations.

dimensions.name: Security & Privacy
dimensions.evidence: Public-safety scanner, env hygiene, prompt-injection fixtures, no raw prompt analytics, and dependency audit command are present.
dimensions.gap: Production secret scoping, environment isolation, and rotation evidence still need verification in the deployed beta environment.
dimensions.nextProof: Verify Vercel environment scopes and document secret-rotation evidence for beta.

dimensions.name: Maintainability
dimensions.evidence: Most durable content lives in structured files with TypeScript exports and validators across content, routes, links, publishing, and Ask.
dimensions.gap: Some UI-local support arrays remain where they are not yet worth extracting.
dimensions.nextProof: Move only the arrays that improve publishing governance, retrieval quality, or review speed.

dimensions.name: Publication Quality
dimensions.evidence: Canonical doctrine, reference architecture, publication pack, evidence pack, glossary, diagrams, PDFs, RSS, and changelog exist.
dimensions.gap: The publication body needs more field-tested examples and reviewer-driven revisions.
dimensions.nextProof: Version doctrine and reference changes only when evidence or practitioner review justifies them.

dimensions.name: Overall Memorability
dimensions.evidence: The Operational Intelligence thesis, Operations Room, Ask Ravikanth, and proof-led professional graph are differentiated.
dimensions.gap: The signature artifact and first impression need more external validation and visual polish before they reliably feel unforgettable.
dimensions.nextProof: Use browser QA and practitioner review to sharpen the first 10 minutes around one memorable evidence-to-decision experience.
